body: CONFIRMED, with bounded blast radius: this is a bench scoring/calibration-path defect, not an HSMM inference defect. `AlignState.isExternal = !isSource`, so `External(Unranked)` is included by `AlignmentRow.externalMass` (matrix.scala:57,132). GraphHsmm makes an abstained/empty candidate set exclusively `Unranked` (hsmm.scala:546), and WorkedExampleSuite proves that row has Unranked mass 1.0 and Intrusion 0.0 (lines 208-233). The sole production consequence traced here is `Metrics.observe` for `open-world:external-over-source`: Association/Intrusion/Uninterpretable gold receives `ind(row.externalMass > row.sourceMass)` (metrics.scala:206-211). Exact counterexample: an unrankable external-gold unit has externalMass=1, sourceMass=0, therefore scores 1.0 despite the aligner having no ranking evidence. That observation is story-macro aggregated into `MetricValue` and rendered under open-world metrics (metrics.scala:289ff; report.scala:228), so it can inflate diagnostic/calibrated benchmark evidence; it does not alter posterior inference. ADR 0003 says hard classifications abstain and explicitly separates Unranked from participant-attributed external content, so the likely correction is metric-side: Unranked rows yield None/explicit missing support (not a positive external decision), with an adversarial regression showing abstention cannot improve external-rule accuracy. No bead or edit made pending chief ruling.
